LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we write apology letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER
This lesson teaches Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter for Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter above.
2. Explain Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write apology letters?
2. what went well and why ● what did not go well and why?
3. what can be done differently next time?
4. what have they learnt?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living
